Does Apple Journal have AI? How it compares with Auserene

faq.q: Is Auserene better than Apple Journal?
faq.a: If you want a journal that does more than hold your writing, yes. Auserene connects quick notes, an evening conversation that writes the entry, a meditation made from your day, memory you can read and edit, people and habit goals, and it has a free plan. Apple Journal is the better pick if you want it free, end-to-end encrypted and on the Mac.

faq.q: Does Apple Journal have an AI chat?
faq.a: No. Apple Journal offers on-device Journaling Suggestions and, on iOS 27 with Apple Intelligence on an iPhone 15 Pro or later, writing prompts based on what you write. Apple's Journal guide doesn't describe a chat, summaries or memory of past entries. Auserene has all three.

faq.q: Is Apple Journal really end-to-end encrypted?
faq.a: Yes. Apple says that with default two-factor authentication and a passcode, all Journal entries are end-to-end encrypted when stored in iCloud, so even Apple can't read them. Auserene is encrypted with AES-256 at rest, using a key unique to you, and travels over TLS, but it is not end-to-end encrypted.

Yes. Apple Journal is free on the App Store for iPhone and iPad, and Apple's Mac guide covers it on macOS Tahoe 26 and later. Auserene also has a free plan with no time limit, and Premium costs $11.99 a month or $105.99 a year with seven days free.

No. It can log your journaling time as Mindful Minutes in the Health app, but it has no guided meditation or breathing. Auserene writes a guided meditation from each evening conversation, has eight guided journeys, and does haptic breathing on Apple Watch.

faq.q: Is there an Apple Journal alternative with AI?
faq.a: Auserene, if you want notes, conversation, meditation, memory, people and goals in one connected app on iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch. Day One's Gold plan, Rosebud, Reflection and Mindsera also use AI. Our Apple Journal alternatives guide compares them.

informationGain: A disclosed head-to-head built from Apple's own iOS 27 and macOS 27 Journal guides and privacy pages on November 19, 2026, including that Writing Prompts need an iPhone 15 Pro or later, voice transcription is English only and entries skip iCloud backups, set against a walkthrough of how Auserene's notes, conversation, meditation, memory, people and goals connect, while conceding plainly that Apple Journal is free and more private.
